description: The Committee Chair provided no verbal report.
Police Service Centre hours extended to 8 AM-8 PM daily.
Saskatoon Police face staffing shortages, impacting proactive work.
Downtown businesses report slow police response due to staffing.

chips.text: Equity and Culture Engagement Unit raised $2259 for Camp Caterpillar summer programming.
Downtown businesses expressed frustration over police response times at a previous meeting.
Chief McBride stated a plan is in place to address rising call volumes and improve presence.

description: Saskatoon Police Service receives positive public feedback.

chips.text: Saskatoon Police Service staff are recognized for their work.
Public feedback describes police as professional, empathetic, and respectful.

speakers.name: Chief McBride
said: We receive much appreciation from the public for our work.
Positive public feedback is shared internally to counter negativity.

description: Saskatoon residents shared feedback on community safety.
Concerns include social disorder, crime, and police capacity.
Feedback will inform the SPS strategic plan, due August.
Some suggestions are already being implemented.

chips.text: Chief McBride committed to considering all community suggestions
Specific solutions for transit safety issues, like a 'transit blitz,' are still under analysis.
Residents expressed compassion for people experiencing poverty, homelessness, mental health

speakers.name: Martell
speakers.summary: Martell presented the matter with a PowerPoint.
said: Residents feel unsafe due to increasing social disorder and crime.
Community partners, SPS programs, and engagement are working well.
Public wants more enforcement, officer visibility, and improved service.
